title: Dilations and Similar Figures
seo_title: Dilations and Similar Figures Worksheet: Scale Factor (Geometry, G-SRT.A.2) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on dilations and similar figures: scale factors, dilations about a center, perimeter and area changes, and similar polygons. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A dilation multiplies every length by the scale factor k.
key_sub: Perimeter changes by k; area changes by k².
body_html:
How it works

A dilation with center C and scale factor k moves every point along the ray from C, so its distance from C is multiplied by k. If k > 1 it is an enlargement; if 0 < k < 1 it is a reduction.

  • Center at the origin: (x, y) → (kx, ky).
  • Another center C: find the step from C to the point, multiply it by k, and add it to C.

Dilations keep angles the same and multiply every length by k, so the image is similar to the original. Perimeters multiply by k, but areas multiply by k².

Example

Dilate (6, 2) by a scale factor of 3 with center (2, 0).

Step from the center: (4, 2)

Times 3: (12, 6)

Add to (2, 0)

Answer: (14, 6)

Example

A triangle with area 20 is dilated by a scale factor of 3. Find the new area.

Area scales by 3² = 9

Answer: 180

Common mistakes

  • Adding the scale factor to the coordinates. Multiply instead.
  • Dilating from the origin when the center is another point.
  • Multiplying area by k. Area changes by k².
  • Writing the proportion upside down. Keep the same figure on top on both sides.

faq.q: What is a dilation in geometry?
faq.a: A transformation that enlarges or reduces a figure by a scale factor from a center point. The image is similar to the original.

faq.q: How do you dilate a point about the origin?
faq.a: Multiply both coordinates by the scale factor: (x, y) → (kx, ky).

faq.q: How does a dilation change area?
faq.a: Area is multiplied by the square of the scale factor. A scale factor of 3 makes the area 9 times as large.
No, unless the scale factor is 1. They are similar: same angles, proportional sides.

items.q: A dilation centered at the origin maps A(−8, −2) to A′(−4, −1). What is the scale factor?
items.e: Divide an image coordinate by the original: −4 ÷ (−8) = 12.

items.q: A figure is dilated by a scale factor of 2. Is the image an enlargement or a reduction?
items.e: A scale factor greater than 1 makes the image larger. An enlargement.

items.e: Multiply both coordinates by 2: (2 × 7, 2 × 7) = (14, 14).

items.q: A polygon has perimeter 22. It is dilated by a scale factor of 2. What is the perimeter of the image?
items.e: Perimeter is a length, so it is multiplied by 2: 44.

items.q: A segment of length 24 is dilated by a scale factor of 32. How long is the image?
items.e: Lengths are multiplied by the scale factor: 32 × 24 = 36.

items.q: Two similar figures have corresponding sides in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the ratio of their areas?
items.e: The ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of sides: 2² : 3² = 4 : 9.

items.q: Two similar figures have corresponding sides in the ratio 3 : 2. What is the ratio of their areas?

items.q: A side of length 13 becomes 26 after a dilation. What is the scale factor?

items.q: Ethan enlarges a 4 in. by 6 in. photo so that the short side is 8 in. How long is the long side?
items.e: The scale factor is 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Long side = 2 × 6 = 12 in.

items.q: A model ship is built at a scale of 1 : 64. The model is 5 ft long. How long is the real ship?
items.e: Every real length is 64 times the model length: 64 × 5 = 320 ft.

items.q: A 10-inch pizza and a 15-inch pizza are similar circles. How many times as much pizza is the larger one?
items.e: Areas scale by the square of the ratio: (15 ÷ 10)² = 225 ÷ 100 = 94.
